newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine telecom rates unchanged by courts-agency.
newsitem.headline: Argentine telecom rates unchanged by courts-agency.

text.p: One of Argentina's two big telecommunications companies said Friday it continued to charge new rates authorized by the government despite conflicting court rulings.

The latest in a string of court orders came Thursday, when one judge ordered telephone companies to scrap a new set of tariffs ordered by the government, and a second judge ordered that the new rates be maintained.

But a spokesman for Telefonica de Argentina said the company had still not been formally notified of any court rulings and so was keeping the new tariffs authorized by government decree late in January.
"Today, the tariffs applied are those which were ordered by the Communications Secretariat, which are the restructured tariffs," the spokesman told Reuters.
Thursday's decisions were the latest in a volley of court rulings on the tariff changes, which have become a legal football since authorized by decree late in January.
The changes increased the cost of local calls and telephone rentals but slashed the rates for national and international long distance calls.

Telefonica de Argentina and Telecom Argentina had waged a long lobbying campaign for the tariff changes, which they said would make charges fairer for provincial businesses. They also hoped it would make them more competitive when the Argentine phone market is thrown open to all competition, probably in the year 2000.

But consumer groups and opposition parties fought hard against the charges and argued in public hearings ending in December 1996 that private users' telephone bills would rise and the phone companies pocket the difference.
The companies argued the new charges would not increase their profits. Telefonica is controlled by Telefonica de Espana, and Telecom by France Telecom.
